claims.hypothesis: Larger complex organic molecules beyond methanol and formaldehyde are present in the gas phase in the IRS 48 asymmetric dust trap due to ice sublimation.
claims.experiment: Imaged ALMA Band 7 line data with tclean using a Keplerian mask, stacked disk-integrated spectra with GoFish, and performed LTE spectral modelling with CASSIS.
claims.result: Detected two sets of blended lines of dimethyl ether (N = 1.5 x 10^15 cm^-2 at 100 K), tentatively detected methyl formate (N = 1.3 x 10^15 cm^-2 at 100 K), and detected five transitions of nitric oxide (at T_ex = 40 K), all spatially associated with the southern dust trap.
claims.finding: Dimethyl ether and nitric oxide are detected for the first time in a protoplanetary disk alongside tentative methyl formate, directly linked to the icy dust trap.

evidence.loc: Detection of dimethyl ether and methyl formate
evidence.quote: We detect two sets of blended lines for .

The emissions of the detected species show a direct link with the asymmetric dust trap in the southern region of the disk, further suggesting that molecular complexity in this disk is due to ice sublimation.

claims.hypothesis: Strong methanol lines in IRS 48 may be optically thick and beam diluted, causing previous analyses to underestimate the methanol column density.
claims.experiment: Modelled newly identified weak CH3OH transitions (at 351.236 GHz and 361.236 GHz) and the 13CH3OH isotopologue upper limit in the GoFish-stacked spectra using CASSIS.
claims.result: The two weak CH3OH lines are better fit with N(CH3OH) = 2 x 10^15 cm^-2 at 100 K (higher than the 5 x 10^14 cm^-2 fit to stronger lines), consistent with the 13CH3OH upper limit (< 5.5 x 10^14 cm^-2, implying N(CH3OH) < 3.3 x 10^16 cm^-2).
claims.finding: Stronger CH3OH lines are likely optically thick and beam diluted, implying a smaller true emitting area (such as a thin crescent at the inner edge of the dust cavity) or enhanced COM/CH3OH ratios.

evidence.quote: We also detect two weaker lines in the stacked spectra that are better fit at a higher column density of 2 $\times$ cm$^{-2}$ and still at a temperature of 100 K (see Figure 2 for a comparison of the two models).
The difference between this and our result can be resolved if the lines are optically thick and beam diluted, because the column density is inversely proportional to the assumed emitting area.
We also derived a 3$\sigma$ upper limit for the column density of of $<$ 5.5 $\times 10^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$.

claims.hypothesis: The complex organic molecules in IRS 48 originate from cold grain-surface chemistry inherited from the parent molecular cloud, possibly modified by UV irradiation in the disk.
claims.experiment: Compared derived abundance ratios of CH3OCH3, CH3OCHO, and CH3OH in IRS 48 with Class 0 protostars (IRAS 16293 A/B), the outbursting source V883 Ori, and comet 67P.
claims.result: The CH3OCHO / CH3OCH3 ratio is ~0.9, matching other environments from protostars to comets, whereas the ratios of both species relative to CH3OH are higher by a factor of 5-10.
claims.finding: The consistent CH3OCHO / CH3OCH3 ratio supports a shared ice formation route inherited from the cold cloud phase, while the high ratios relative to CH3OH reflect either underestimated optically thick CH3OH or UV-driven enhancement in the disk ice trap.

evidence.quote: The / ratio in our disk is approximately 0.9 and this is consistent with what is observed in other sources across a full range of environments from star and disk formation to comets (cite: coletta2020evolutionary).
The high observed / ratio in the IRS 48 disk, of order unity, is different from that in the other sources by a factor of 5-10 (Figure [3](#fig:barplots)).

The detection of and in such a warm disk and the agreement in the / column density ratio with other environments strengthens the case for an origin inherited from the cold cloud phase, but the abundances with respect to may be enhanced because of UV irradiation.

why_this_data.value: IRS 48 is a warm Herbig transition disk with a highly asymmetric dust trap of large grains where icy COMs sublimate into the gas phase and become observable with ALMA.

evidence.quote: Also, another Herbig source was revealed to have a rich observable chemistry: the IRS 48 transition disk (cite: van2014warm; van2021major; booth2021major).

The bulk of the ice reservoir of the IRS48 disk is constrained to the larger dust grains, and because of UV irradiation from the central star, the dust temperature increases enough to liberate the from the ices.

referee_caveats_inferred: Extracting the spectrum over the full 360-degree azimuth with GoFish while assuming the 5-sigma dust continuum crescent area for column density conversion could introduce a mismatch between the flux extraction aperture and the assumed emitting solid angle if not scaled consistently.
The methyl formate assignment relies heavily on one blended feature at 363.48-363.49 GHz where the LTE model does not match the exact profile shape.
Degeneracy between optical depth and beam dilution in CH3OH cannot be broken without higher angular resolution observations or a detection of 13CH3OH.
